methodology: CFC browser screenshot of Keepa price charts -> base64 PNG -> Gemini 2.0 Flash vision API

gemini_response_full_screenshot.price_trend: Relatively stable, trending slightly upwards towards the end of the chart

results.notes: Cropped chart gave more detailed price points than full screenshot

gemini_response.lowest_price: Approximately $40, based on the lowest point on the 'New' price line (purple) within the visible time frame.
gemini_response.highest_price: Approximately $60, based on the highest point on the 'New' price line (purple) within the visible time frame.
gemini_response.price_trend: Generally stable with some fluctuations, but primarily flat since February

results.notes: Current price $59.99 matches Keepa header. Chart shows stable pricing around $48-60.

feasibility: FEASIBLE BUT LIMITED. Gemini can read Keepa charts and extract approximate price points, date ranges, and trends. However, precision is limited to ~$2-5 per reading and ~1 week date accuracy. The 3-month default view gives recent history but misses long-term data. Better results from cropped chart images vs full screenshots. Main limitations: (1) approximate readings only - not exact cents, (2) date precision limited to weeks, (3) requires browser automation for each ASIN, (4) Keepa Pro subscription required for chart access, (5) chart interactivity (hover for exact values) not captured in static screenshots.
estimated_cost_per_asin: $0.001-0.002 (Gemini 2.0 Flash: ~650KB image input + ~200 token output per request at Gemini pricing). Screenshot overhead: ~5-8 seconds per ASIN for page load + screenshot.
accuracy_assessment: MODERATE. For the FC11C, Gemini identified the price range ($0-$50) and date range (Jan-Apr) correctly. It found approximate highs and lows but readings varied between full vs cropped chart attempts (e.g., current price reported as $42 vs $35). For the HD01 UV, it correctly identified $59.99 current price from the header text. Price point readings are approximate to ~$5 precision. Trend assessment (stable/volatile) is reliable. For our torch pipeline use case (filling price_usd field), the Keepa API direct data would be far more precise -- this vision approach is a creative workaround but not production-grade for exact pricing.
comparison_to_api: Keepa API returns exact prices with timestamps. Vision approach returns approximate readings (~$5 precision). API: 1 token/product, 60/hour limit. Vision: no Keepa token cost but ~$0.002 Gemini cost + browser automation overhead. API is strictly superior for data quality.
recommendation: Use Keepa API for price data extraction. Vision approach is a viable fallback for occasional spot-checks or when API tokens are exhausted, but not suitable for bulk pipeline use due to imprecision and browser automation overhead.
